ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Voltaire — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Two-week review during weekly radiotherapy: symptoms, kidney function, voiding, and opioid safety

text.paragraph: Voltaire returns two weeks after starting the pain plan. He had the first radiotherapy fraction a week ago and the second this morning. Since the first fraction he has passed urine more often, about every two hours by day and twice at night, with mild burning, but the stream is steady and there have been no clots; the urine is pale pink on some days. He takes acetaminophen three times a day and has used eight half tablets of oxycodone in fourteen days, mostly in the evening, with good relief and no drowsiness, confusion, or falls; seven tablets remain in the locked box, and he has taken nothing else for pain or sleep. His bowels open daily on polyethylene glycol and senna. The palliative care team visited him at home last week. The physical therapist from the wellness visit has not yet come. He has lost 0.5 kg and drinks the supplement once a day. He wrote every morning this week. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1778-05-06; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Thin, alert, and lively; not drowsy; pupils normal size
Blood pressure 122/68 mmHg; heart rate 80, regular
Soft; mild suprapubic tenderness; bladder not palpable
No skin reaction over the pelvis
Visible blood in the urine for three weeks with clots, and a weak stream, straining, and frequent small voids, in a man of 83; under evaluation
S — Synthetic presenting problem echoing his documented urinary complaints and last illness; superseded by the diagnosis at the third chronic-care visit.
Chronic urinary retention with overflow (post-void residual 460 mL at intake), worsened by a nightly anticholinergic sleep aid; drained by an indwelling catheter
S — Synthetic finding echoing the strangury and catheterization documented in his last weeks.
Acute kidney injury from bladder outlet obstruction (creatinine 1.68 mg/dL, from 1.1 mg/dL a year earlier)
S — Synthetic finding; it echoes, without asserting, the later encyclopedia term uremia.

Benign prostatic hyperplasia with lower urinary tract symptoms: prostate about 78 mL on CT, enlarged, firm, and smooth on examination, PSA 6.4 ng/mL with a PSA density of 0.08; no prostate biopsy, by shared decision
S — Synthetic diagnosis echoing the very large prostate described at the 1778 autopsy; whether that prostate was malignant is unknown (CLM-0012).

Squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder, keratinizing, posterior wall extending to the dome, muscle-invasive with extravesical extension (clinical stage cT3b N0 M0, stage IIIA), pure squamous histology without a urothelial component; treated with palliative-intent hypofractionated radiotherapy by shared decision

S — Synthetic modern diagnosis confirmed by resection pathology. His bladder disease at autopsy is documented (D); calling it squamous cell carcinoma is a 2025 retrospective interpretation (R, disputed).
Chronic constipation, lifelong by his account, with long use of laxatives and self-given enemas
S — Synthetic modern problem echoing his documented colic, purges, and enemas; no diagnosis of inflammatory bowel disease is made.
Febrile catheter-associated urinary tract infection with Escherichia coli, five days after bladder tumor resection; treated with cefpodoxime and a catheter change; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent infection; it echoes, without asserting, the infected urine described in his last weeks (CLM-0009).

list.item:
Squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder, on weekly radiotherapy (C67.4). Two of six fractions given, with grade 1 radiation cystitis (frequency, nocturia, mild burning) and no grade 2 or higher effects. Bleeding is controlled. Hemoglobin 10.8 g/dL, white count 6.9, platelets 231, and creatinine 1.20 mg/dL (eGFR 60) are stable. The pain plan works: pain 2 of 10 with about one half tablet of oxycodone a day, without sedation or constipation. [S]
Continue weekly radiotherapy to six fractions.
Continue acetaminophen; oxycodone 2.5 mg as needed, the same limits; no new prescription needed yet.
The palliative care team will keep visiting at home.

Chronic urinary retention (R33.8). Post-void residual 120 mL, stable; IPSS 15 with radiation frequency. [S]
Continue tamsulosin; bladder scan at the next visit.

Chronic constipation (K59.09). Controlled on polyethylene glycol and senna while on oxycodone. [S]
No change.

Benign prostatic hyperplasia (N40.1). Symptoms explained by radiation and the enlarged prostate; no dizziness on tamsulosin. [S]
No change.
